before.supportingExcerpt: Residual tumour here means cancer remaining in the sampled tissue after treatment. For residual-tumour research, first support malignant-cell identity, then ask which recovered states, target messages and immune profiles are present. A stress programme does not establish a genetic clone or explain survival. In Kim and colleagues' twenty-person triple-negative breast-cancer study, longitudinal exome data and single-cell DNA/RNA data in eight participants supported selection of pre-existing genotypes alongside expression reprogramming under the studied treatment. This is not a universal resistance mechanism. Compare the sampled region, time, preparation, recovery and analysis before attributing a difference to treatment; a missing cluster need not have been eliminated. In a separate fictional calculation, an input suspension truly containing 4 percent malignant nuclei gives an expectation of 240 among 6,000 retained profiles only if malignant and other nuclei have equal inclusion through recovery, capture and quality filtering. Tissue-area cellularity is a different denominator. The calculation is neither a yield forecast nor an adequacy cutoff.
before.explanation: Residual tissue is sampled after treatment, with identity/state/clone and recovery separated. The20-person Kim study,8 with single-cell analyses, supports its studied longitudinal inference rather than a universal mechanism. Different preparations/regions or a matched pair alone cannot establish why cells survived or a treatment-caused difference. after.supportingExcerpt: Residual tumour here means cancer remaining in the sampled tissue after treatment. For residual-tumour research, first support malignant-cell identity, then ask which recovered states, target messages and immune profiles are present. A stress programme does not establish a genetic clone or explain survival. In Kim and colleagues' twenty-person triple-negative breast-cancer study, longitudinal exome data and single-cell DNA/RNA data in eight participants supported selection of pre-existing genotypes alongside expression reprogramming under the studied treatment. This is not a universal resistance mechanism. Compare the sampled region, time, preparation, recovery and analysis before attributing a difference to treatment; a missing cluster need not have been eliminated. In a separate fictional calculation, an input suspension truly containing 4 percent malignant nuclei gives an expectation of 240 among 6,000 retained profiles only if malignant and other nuclei have equal inclusion through recovery, capture and quality filtering. Tissue-area cellularity is a different denominator. The calculation is neither a yield forecast nor an adequacy cutoff.

before.supportingExcerpt: A detection fraction uses the analysed profiles and a stated detection rule: it is not automatically the fraction of all cells in the original tissue. A profile with one immune-gene count but otherwise epithelial features is not thereby identified as an immune cell. Sparse recovery, ambient RNA and more than one contributing cell can complicate its interpretation. Check coherent marker evidence and the method of assignment; a mixture of markers does not by itself establish a new cell type. Pooling the counts from a selected set of profiles is pseudobulk. Five hundred nuclei from one biopsy can summarize that selected population, while the biopsy remains one biological specimen rather than five hundred independent patients.

before.supportingExcerpt: A detection fraction uses the analysed profiles and a stated detection rule: it is not automatically the fraction of all cells in the original tissue. Check coherent marker evidence and the method of assignment; a mixture of markers does not by itself establish a new cell type. Pooling the counts from a selected set of profiles is pseudobulk. before.supportingExcerpt: Residual tumour here means cancer remaining in the sampled tissue after treatment. For residual-tumour research, first support malignant-cell identity, then ask which recovered states, target messages and immune profiles are present. A stress programme does not establish a genetic clone or explain survival. In Kim and colleagues' twenty-person triple-negative breast-cancer study, longitudinal exome data and single-cell DNA/RNA data in eight participants supported selection of pre-existing genotypes alongside expression reprogramming under the studied treatment. This is not a universal resistance mechanism. Compare the sampled region, time, preparation, recovery and analysis before attributing a difference to treatment; a missing cluster need not have been eliminated. In a separate fictional calculation, an input suspension truly containing 4 percent malignant nuclei gives an expectation of 240 among 6,000 retained profiles only if malignant and other nuclei have equal inclusion through recovery, capture and quality filtering. Tissue-area cellularity is a different denominator. The calculation is neither a yield forecast nor an adequacy cutoff.

Five hundred nuclei from one biopsy can summarize that selected population, while the biopsy remains one biological specimen rather than five hundred independent patients.

before.supportingExcerpt: Residual tumour here means cancer remaining in the sampled tissue after treatment. For residual-tumour research, first support malignant-cell identity, then ask which recovered states, target messages and immune profiles are present. A stress programme does not establish a genetic clone or explain survival. In Kim and colleagues' twenty-person triple-negative breast-cancer study, longitudinal exome data and single-cell DNA/RNA data in eight participants supported selection of pre-existing genotypes alongside expression reprogramming under the studied treatment. This is not a universal resistance mechanism. Compare the sampled region, time, preparation, recovery and analysis before attributing a difference to treatment; a missing cluster need not have been eliminated. In a separate fictional calculation, an input suspension truly containing 4 percent malignant nuclei gives an expectation of 240 among 6,000 retained profiles only if malignant and other nuclei have equal inclusion through recovery, capture and quality filtering. Tissue-area cellularity is a different denominator. The calculation is neither a yield forecast nor an adequacy cutoff.

before.supportingExcerpt: Residual tumour here means cancer remaining in the sampled tissue after treatment. For residual-tumour research, first support malignant-cell identity, then ask which recovered states, target messages and immune profiles are present. A stress programme does not establish a genetic clone or explain survival. In Kim and colleagues' twenty-person triple-negative breast-cancer study, longitudinal exome data and single-cell DNA/RNA data in eight participants supported selection of pre-existing genotypes alongside expression reprogramming under the studied treatment. This is not a universal resistance mechanism. Compare the sampled region, time, preparation, recovery and analysis before attributing a difference to treatment; a missing cluster need not have been eliminated. In a separate fictional calculation, an input suspension truly containing 4 percent malignant nuclei gives an expectation of 240 among 6,000 retained profiles only if malignant and other nuclei have equal inclusion through recovery, capture and quality filtering. Tissue-area cellularity is a different denominator. The calculation is neither a yield forecast nor an adequacy cutoff.

A stress programme does not establish a genetic clone or explain survival. In Kim and colleagues' twenty-person triple-negative breast-cancer study, longitudinal exome data and single-cell DNA/RNA data in eight participants supported selection of pre-existing genotypes alongside expression reprogramming under the studied treatment. This is not a universal resistance mechanism. Compare the sampled region, time, preparation, recovery and analysis before attributing a difference to treatment; a missing cluster need not have been eliminated. In a separate fictional calculation, an input suspension truly containing 4 percent malignant nuclei gives an expectation of 240 among 6,000 retained profiles only if malignant and other nuclei have equal inclusion through recovery, capture and quality filtering. Tissue-area cellularity is a different denominator. The calculation is neither a yield forecast nor an adequacy cutoff.

Check coherent marker evidence and the method of assignment; a mixture of markers does not by itself establish a new cell type. Pooling the counts from a selected set of profiles is pseudobulk. before.supportingExcerpt: Residual tumour here means cancer remaining in the sampled tissue after treatment. For residual-tumour research, first support malignant-cell identity, then ask which recovered states, target messages and immune profiles are present. A stress programme does not establish a genetic clone or explain survival. In Kim and colleagues' twenty-person triple-negative breast-cancer study, longitudinal exome data and single-cell DNA/RNA data in eight participants supported selection of pre-existing genotypes alongside expression reprogramming under the studied treatment. This is not a universal resistance mechanism. Compare the sampled region, time, preparation, recovery and analysis before attributing a difference to treatment; a missing cluster need not have been eliminated. In a separate fictional calculation, an input suspension truly containing 4 percent malignant nuclei gives an expectation of 240 among 6,000 retained profiles only if malignant and other nuclei have equal inclusion through recovery, capture and quality filtering. Tissue-area cellularity is a different denominator. The calculation is neither a yield forecast nor an adequacy cutoff.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Support a malignant-cell assignment with tissue context, a coherent marker panel, suitable normal references and quality checks, rather than one marker or cluster name. In five primary glioblastomas, Patel and colleagues profiled 430 cells and inferred broad chromosome alterations by averaging RNA expression along chromosomes against normal reference profiles. This was RNA-based inference, not a direct DNA copy count or a breast diagnostic rule. A flat inferred profile can miss a malignant cell lacking a detectable broad change; focal alterations and point mutations can also be missed. Matched DNA, pathology and spatial evidence can corroborate an assignment, but bulk DNA does not identify every RNA barcode. Mixed markers may reflect ambient RNA or doublets. points.requirement: In the RNA example, removal of introns joins retained exons1,2,3. This is processing of a transcript, not deletion or rewriting of the genomic DNA.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Splicing processes an initial RNA transcript. Exons are retained in a specified product and may contain untranslated sequence; introns are removed. Alternative choices yield transcript isoforms; a variant can alter exon inclusion, intron retention or use of a cryptic site. An altered message may undergo nonsense-mediated decay or produce a changed protein, but neither outcome follows from a prediction alone.
